text: {"rationale": "Rule C-25 requires the NDA to permit copies for backup, disaster recovery and legally required records. Segment 6 expressly requires return of all copies and records on request and says the Recipient will not retain any copies or records, with no carve-out for backup or legal retention in the segments shown. Segment 12 limits copying to the Purpose only. The clause 4 exceptions shown only lift the use and disclosure undertakings in clauses 2 and 3, not the return and retention obligation in clause 6, so the finding that the NDA does not permit these copies is supported.", "verdict": "supported", "confidence": 0.85}

{"rationale": "Segment 3 limits use to the Transaction and bars any other purpose without written consent, and segment 4a bars any use or any manufacture or testing of products embodying the information except for the stated purpose. Those cover the product development exclusion in substance. Quoting to customers and staff training are not named expressly, but segment 4a's general no-use wording and the need-to-know limit in segment 38a support the restriction in substance.", "label": "Entailment", "evidence": [45, 54], "confidence": 0.7}

{"rationale": "The rule requires an exemption for legally required records and signed-agreement copies from any return or destruction obligation. None of the shown segments contains such an exemption in any wording. Segment 31 refers to return of Confidential Information only in a survival sentence, so the omission finding is supported, though the shown segments are an excerpt and the NDA's full return clause is not visible.", "verdict": "supported", "confidence": 0.7}

{"rationale": "A residuals clause would be an express permission to keep using remembered information, and this NDA contains none. Segment 19 restricts all use of Confidential Information to the Purpose, which is the opposite of a residuals permission. The finding's reading that the use restriction itself breaches the rule is not supported, since a restriction on use does not let the other side keep using remembered information.", "verdict": "unsupported", "confidence": 0.8}

{"rationale": "Segment 19 bars disclosure to any third party without written approval, but the Receiving Party's own employees are not normally third parties, and segment 22 makes the party answerable for its employees, which implies they may receive the information. The finding and a plain reading of the text could go either way.", "verdict": "uncertain", "confidence": 0.5}
